paper.title_en: New Analytic Methods in Black Hole Perturbation Theory
paper.abstract_en:
Motivated by the steady developments in gravitational-wave astronomy, this dis-
sertation focuses on the analytical aspects of black hole perturbation theory. We
present novel analytical techniques that deal with quasinormal modes (QNMs)
and scattering amplitudes of black holes.
Like a string or a bell, black holes tend to vibrate at the lowest possible frequency
or the fundamental frequency. These fundamental frequencies are known numer-
ically, but the analytic description or the mathematical tools necessary for their
understanding are not fully developed. In the first part of the dissertation, we
present one such tool, which utilizes the connection between equations describing
small perturbations of ordinary black holes and Seiberg-Witten theory.
In the next part, we investigate the vibrations of black holes embedded in four-
dimensional spacetime with negative or positive cosmological constant. In the
case of the negative cosmological constant, the Seiberg-Witten approach proves
to be more complicated to implement, and we propose an alternative method to set up perturbation theory for both small and large black holes in an analytical
manner. We reveal a new underlying recursive structure that involves multiple
polylogarithms.
In the final part of the dissertation, we introduce a novel approach to black
hole scattering amplitudes based on a new set of special functions called multiple
polyexponential integrals. By solving the Regge-Wheeler equation perturbatively
in the small-frequency regime, we determine the monodromy in the near-spatial
infinity region and derive a specific partial diﬀerential equation on the elements
of the scattering matrix. As a result, we pinpoint the exact form of scattering
amplitudes in Schwarzschild spacetime.
